bug_semantics: An authenticated non-site-admin user with perm_template could request the event-template add page (or edit a writable template), causing EventTemplatesController::__setBuilderConfig() to fetch every enabled Galaxy row without the Galaxy visibility conditions. The resulting galaxy type and description values were JSON-embedded in window.ET_BUILDER_CONFIG, disclosing private, organisation-only galaxy metadata belonging to other organisations.
flaw_origin: Commit 47bf71cc78d13c06e1eaa4d9842e6f94ddce4bea introduced the galaxy-type picker and its server-side Galaxy::find('all') query with only 'Galaxy.enabled' => true. It created the data source and browser-visible sink together but omitted the existing organisation/distribution visibility policy; its immediate parent had neither galaxyTypesAvailable nor this Galaxy query.
evidence: In the validated clone, `git show --format=fuller 47bf71cc78d13c06e1eaa4d9842e6f94ddce4bea -- app/Controller/EventTemplatesController.php` shows the new __setBuilderConfig() block querying Galaxy with `conditions => array('Galaxy.enabled' => true)` and selecting Galaxy.type/Galaxy.description. `git grep -n '__setBuilderConfig\|public function add\|public function edit' 47bf71cc... -- app/Controller/EventTemplatesController.php` locates GET-path calls at lines 126 and 174, while the same commit's ACLComponent maps add/edit to perm_template rather than site-admin. `git show 47bf71cc...:app/View/Elements/eventTemplates/builder/shell.ctp` shows galaxyTypesAvailable entering multipickerSources at lines 35-38 and JSON encoding into window.ET_BUILDER_CONFIG at line 340. `git log --all -S"'conditions' => array('Galaxy.enabled' => true)" -- app/Controller/EventTemplatesController.php` identifies 47bf71cc... as the addition (and d3adfe1a... as its later removal); `git log 47bf71cc... -L 664,700:app/Controller/EventTemplatesController.php` likewise attributes the vulnerable block to 47bf71cc.... `git rev-parse 47bf71cc...^` returns 66f278bb2be0e8183d56eede615d7cc370f38303, and `git grep -n 'galaxyTypesAvailable\|Galaxy.enabled' 66f278bb... -- app/Controller/EventTemplatesController.php app/View/Elements/eventTemplates/builder/shell.ctp` exits 1 with no matches, directly verifying parent absence. `git cat-file -p 47bf71cc...` shows a single parent, human author/committer iglocska, and the exact Claude Co-Authored-By trailer quoted in ai_marker; no decomposition is needed because this ordinary single-parent commit itself adds the vulnerable lines. The advisory-linked d3adfe1a097dd4b403364e9af34e208660eeec1a attempted a restriction, but `git show d3adfe1a...` shows the malformed array item `'Galaxy.distribution' > 0`; PHP evaluates that comparison to true instead of forming a database predicate, so the OR condition remains universally true. `git show 8aa2bb6d1af6e8c57c8d8437cf203acb8bce7a53` removes that ineffective condition and calls `$this->Galaxy->buildConditions($this->Auth->user())`; app/Model/Galaxy.php:689-705 defines that canonical helper to allow site-admins and otherwise restrict by default galaxy, caller org_id, or non-private distribution. Release ancestry is explicit: `git tag --contains 47bf71cc...` starts at v2.5.37; v2.5.36 target b75a2ff90b8f5ec40699a84796bd729406a5f975 does not contain it, while v2.5.37 target be735cf3e9e61c81e8122b52ef70970b084dc872 does. d3adfe1a... first appears in v2.5.39, but 8aa2bb6d... is absent from v2.5.39 target 82e9c4f22879e3f32f60f5857aac0e829152bc76 and first appears in v2.5.40 target 57ec6febfd1adab7a58038def39a76c19ce0cbeb. Direct `git show v2.5.39:app/Controller/EventTemplatesController.php` retains the malformed comparison; v2.5.40 uses buildConditions. Thus v2.5.37 through v2.5.39 are affected, and v2.5.40 is the first actually fixed release.
reasoning: The vulnerable capability did not exist in the immediate parent. The BIC added both the all-enabled-galaxies query and the client-visible picker payload, so it is the smallest causal introduction rather than a move, refactor, release commit, or later aggregate. Any perm_template non-site-admin reaching add/edit could receive metadata from another organisation's distribution-0 custom galaxy. Although the advisory points to d3adfe1a097dd4b403364e9af34e208660eeec1a, that commit's intended distribution predicate is a PHP comparison and does not constrain the query, leaving v2.5.39 vulnerable. Commit 8aa2bb6d1af6e8c57c8d8437cf203acb8bce7a53 is the real closing fix because it replaces the broken hand-written condition with Galaxy::buildConditions(), and its first containing release is v2.5.40. The BIC commit object itself explicitly co-authors Claude Opus 4.7, and that same BIC first writes the flawed mechanism; under the protocol this is AI_ROOT_CAUSE, independent of any later commit or external disclosure.
